Sudowrite

AI writing tool built specifically for fiction.

OverviewFeaturesUse casesPricingTradeoffsCompatibilityFAQ

What is Sudowrite?

AI writing tool built specifically for fiction. Rather than generating finished prose, it offers craft-oriented tools - Describe, Brainstorm, Expand, Rewrite, Twist - designed to break through blocks and deepen scenes while the author stays in control.

Best for

Fiction drafting assistance that preserves the author's voice.

Main features

  • Story Bible (characters, worldbuilding, outline, style) that grounds all generation
  • Describe (sensory detail for a scene)
  • Brainstorm (idea generation)
  • Expand and Rewrite
  • Twist (plot turns)
  • Muse model tuned for fiction prose
  • Canvas plotting board
  • chapter continuity tracking
  • no-training-on-your-work policy.

Practical use cases

  • Getting unstuck mid-chapter
  • generating sensory description for a setting
  • exploring alternative plot directions
  • maintaining character and worldbuilding consistency across a long manuscript
  • rewriting a flat paragraph.

Who is it for?

  • Novelists, short-story writers, screenwriters, NaNoWriMo participants, genre and indie authors.

Pricing, free access & limits

Credit-based subscription

Plans described in the source

Hobby & Student around $19/mo (roughly 225,000 credit-words/month). Professional around $29/mo (roughly 1,000,000 credit-words). Max around $59/mo (roughly 2,000,000 credit-words). Annual billing discounts apply. Credits are consumed by generation, with the Muse model costing more per word than standard models.

Free plan

No free plan.

Free trial

Yes - a free trial with a limited credit allowance (historically around 3,000 credit-words), no card required.

Usage limits to consider

Credit-word metered per month, with premium models consuming credits faster. Unused credits generally do not roll over.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The only tool in this list designed by and for fiction writers - the craft vocabulary (Describe, Twist) matches how authors actually work
  • Story Bible grounding keeps long manuscripts consistent
  • explicit policy of not training on user manuscripts
  • Muse produces noticeably less generic prose than general models.

Limitations to consider

  • Narrow - almost useless for non-fiction or business writing
  • credit pricing is confusing and premium models drain it fast
  • browser-only with no offline mode
  • controversial within parts of the writing community, which may matter for authors publicly positioning against AI
  • no collaboration features.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web (browser-based editor)

Languages

  • Primarily English; other languages supported but the craft tools are tuned for English prose

API access

No public API

Integrations and exports

  • Import/export DOCX and Markdown
  • Scrivener import
  • Google Docs via copy-paste

Evaluation notes

Best used as a thinking aid rather than a prose generator - authors who accept raw output wholesale produce noticeably flatter work. The Story Bible is the feature that makes the difference on a full-length manuscript.
